channel.title: Zuru&Obi on Srikanth Perinkulam

item.description:
We finally made it to Ebogo this morning! Been on our list for a while now but for some reason it never materialized. About 55 kms from home with the last 7 kms through unpaved road - Getting there was super straight forward.

Alexis our guide greeted us cheerfully and quickly got us into the Padauk pirogues. Skirting the corners, he moved us upstream steadily for about 90 minutes.

With abundant monsoon this season, River Nyong was at about 26ft apparently. Summer is right round the corner and he doesn’t anticipate it reaching it’s peak average depth of 40ft.

Parts of the forest were submerged and he took us into the woods. Weaving into and out of these trees was pretty awesome! You could feel a sudden drop in temperature here.

As we made our way out of the forest and back into main river, Alexis mentioned he’d seen a documentary about the dowry system in India and that he kept telling his wife he should have gotten married there instead. The groom pays the bride’s family in this part of the world!

Once out of the woods, Alexis steered us across the river towards the northwest and for a quick shore stop at Kossipo. The magnificent Kossipo tree believed to be ~1200 years old spans about 25-30ft in diameter and punches up to about 280ft high! We got some quick bites from those large black ants on the way up to the tree. On the way back S&I made sure we ran as quickly as we could.

The return leg from Kossipo was all downstream and we probably got back in about 25 minutes. Grabbed a decent bite at the restaurant and made our way back to Yaounde. I think our GV would have made it in and out but I am glad we got out right before it started raining. Wouldn’t be fun to be stuck in muck! Return was super straight forward following the Organic Maps’ directions. Google maps seems to have taken us through the inner roads for no reason earlier this morning.

Alexis promised he’d let us actually handle the oars if we let him know before hand. So maybe one more trip is due here. Otherwise this was a pretty quick and nice getaway! 🔗
